configureawaitoptions-advanced-await.title: Control advanced await behavior with ConfigureAwaitOptions
configureawaitoptions-advanced-await.short: Choose advanced continuation and exception behavior for an await
configureawaitoptions-advanced-await.summary: ConfigureAwaitOptions exposes advanced await behaviors beyond choosing whether to capture a context, including forced yielding and exception handling options.
configureawaitoptions-advanced-await.why: Low-level async infrastructure and reusable libraries occasionally need finer control than ConfigureAwait(bool) provides.
configureawaitoptions-advanced-await.tips: Prefer ordinary await in application code and use these flags only where their exact semantics are required and documented.

conditionalweaktable-attached-metadata.title: Attach metadata without extending lifetime with ConditionalWeakTable
conditionalweaktable-attached-metadata.short: Let associated data disappear when its key becomes collectible
conditionalweaktable-attached-metadata.summary: ConditionalWeakTable associates external metadata with objects without keeping keys alive solely because the table references them.
conditionalweaktable-attached-metadata.why: It is useful for attaching information to types you cannot modify while avoiding accidental retention caused by a normal Dictionary.
conditionalweaktable-attached-metadata.tips: It is not a general dictionary replacement; choose another structure when enumeration or value-based lookup is central.

memorymappedfile-large-data.title: Work with large files through MemoryMappedFile
memorymappedfile-large-data.short: Map selected file ranges into virtual memory for random access
memorymappedfile-large-data.summary: MemoryMappedFile maps file content into virtual memory so ranges can be accessed without first loading the whole file into a managed byte array.
memorymappedfile-large-data.why: Large datasets and scattered random access can avoid very large managed allocations and unnecessary copying.
memorymappedfile-large-data.tips: Benchmark against FileStream or RandomAccess for the real workload and dispose both views and mappings deterministically.

aspnetcore-rate-limiting.title: Rate-limit requests in ASP.NET Core
aspnetcore-rate-limiting.short: Protect finite resources with the built-in rate limiter
aspnetcore-rate-limiting.summary: ASP.NET Core Rate Limiting Middleware can apply policies such as fixed-window limits to endpoints.
aspnetcore-rate-limiting.why: It helps prevent bursts or excessive traffic from consuming more downstream capacity than the application can safely serve.
aspnetcore-rate-limiting.tips: Design limits around endpoint and caller behavior rather than applying one arbitrary global number, and observe rejected requests.

backgroundservice-scoped-dependencies.title: Do not retain scoped dependencies in BackgroundService
backgroundservice-scoped-dependencies.short: Create scopes that match each unit of background work
backgroundservice-scoped-dependencies.summary: BackgroundService instances are long-lived, so directly retaining scoped services breaks the lifetime assumptions of request-scoped dependencies.
backgroundservice-scoped-dependencies.why: Objects such as DbContext can accumulate state, be used concurrently, or be disposed at the wrong time when kept for the worker lifetime.
backgroundservice-scoped-dependencies.tips: Create an IServiceScope for the appropriate work unit and dispose it when that unit completes.

jsonextensiondata-forward-compatibility.title: Round-trip unknown JSON fields with JsonExtensionData
jsonextensiondata-forward-compatibility.short: Capture fields outside the known model for compatible round trips
jsonextensiondata-forward-compatibility.summary: JsonExtensionData stores JSON properties without matching model members in a designated dictionary.
jsonextensiondata-forward-compatibility.why: Gateways and evolving schemas can preserve fields introduced by newer producers instead of silently dropping them.
jsonextensiondata-forward-compatibility.tips: Treat unknown data as untrusted, set sensible size limits, and decide explicitly whether it should be emitted again.

vector-simd-data-parallelism.title: Use Vector<T> for SIMD data parallelism
vector-simd-data-parallelism.short: Apply one numeric operation to multiple values at once
vector-simd-data-parallelism.summary: System.Numerics.Vector<T> uses the SIMD width available on the runtime to process multiple values with the same operation.
vector-simd-data-parallelism.why: Image, signal, and numeric-array workloads can become faster when they perform regular arithmetic over many elements.
vector-simd-data-parallelism.tips: Handle remainder elements correctly and benchmark against a straightforward loop because the JIT can already optimize some patterns.

dynamicdependency-trimming-contract.title: Preserve trimming dependencies with DynamicDependency
dynamicdependency-trimming-contract.short: Describe dependencies that static analysis cannot see
dynamicdependency-trimming-contract.summary: DynamicDependencyAttribute tells the trimmer that dynamically accessed types or members must remain available.
dynamicdependency-trimming-contract.why: It prevents members referenced only through reflection or similar mechanisms from disappearing during publish-time trimming.
dynamicdependency-trimming-contract.tips: Keep declarations narrow and prefer source generation or DynamicallyAccessedMembers when those express the dependency more naturally.

objectpool-reusable-expensive-objects.title: Reuse expensive temporary objects with ObjectPool
objectpool-reusable-expensive-objects.short: Pool resettable objects that are costly to allocate repeatedly
objectpool-reusable-expensive-objects.summary: ObjectPool<T> lends and returns reusable objects such as StringBuilder to reduce repeated construction on hot paths.
objectpool-reusable-expensive-objects.why: It can lower allocation and GC pressure when large temporary objects are created at high frequency.
objectpool-reusable-expensive-objects.tips: Reset all observable state before return and benchmark to ensure pooling complexity actually produces a useful gain.

dllimportresolver-native-library-routing.title: Route native libraries with DllImportResolver
dllimportresolver-native-library-routing.short: Map a P/Invoke logical name to platform-specific native libraries
dllimportresolver-native-library-routing.summary: NativeLibrary.SetDllImportResolver installs assembly-level logic for resolving native library names.
dllimportresolver-native-library-routing.why: One interop layer can select different library files or locations for different operating systems and deployment layouts.
dllimportresolver-native-library-routing.tips: Verify ABI compatibility and never broaden resolution to untrusted search paths that could load arbitrary native code.
